items.title: Phospholipid remodeling of the cardiomyocyte membrane affects cardiac function
items.author: Issei Komuro
items.content: Cardiomyocyte LPLAT7/LPGAT1 regulates membrane phospholipid composition and cardiac function. Its loss reduces stearic acid- and DHA-enriched phosphatidylcholine and causes PKA activation, abnormal calcium handling, and contractile dysfunction, whereas overexpression partially improves pressure overload-induced dysfunction

items.title: Flippability of Escherichia coli membrane proteins under lipid stress reveals a new job for old genes
items.author: Mikhail Bogdanov
items.content: Altering E. coli lipids disrupts growth, but controlled membrane protein flipping simulates natural selection and resemonstrates that membrane proteins can re-evolve under the selective pressure of an altered lipid bilayer.

items.title: The representation of order and randomness in the auditory cortex
items.author: Israel Nelken
items.content: Neurons in the auditory cortex exhibit a continuum of preferences from order to randomness, and show sensitivity to the position of tones in abstract repeating patterns.
